prompt: You are the test author this time: write isCorrect so it accepts a correct SafeParser and rejects broken ones. Complete the checker in the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: The interesting bug is the null one, because it is a catch block that looks right: Integer.parseInt(text.trim()) throws NullPointerException on a null string, and a catch for NumberFormatException does not catch it. Only an actual null input distinguishes that from correct code. The fallback bug hides too -- if every test uses 0 as the fallback, an implementation that ignores the fallback and returns 0 passes every one of them, which is why the checker must pass a fallback that is not zero and not equal to any expected value.
hints: Pass null as the text. One implementation catches NumberFormatException but null makes .trim() throw NullPointerException, which sails straight past it.
Never use 0 as your fallback in a test: an implementation that returns 0 regardless would pass. Use a value like 5 or 9 and check you get it back.
The contract says whole numbers, so "3.5" must produce the fallback rather than 3.
